title: Bounded-space execution of the comparison program
statement: For any Boolean values $a,b$ and natural numbers $n,i$, for every pair of natural numbers $c,d$ with $c+d=n$ and $c\le i$, the comparison program started in its test state with its sole register equal to $c$ halts on input $\langle 1^n,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle$, returns the Boolean value of $(i<n\text{ and }a=\mathrm{true})$ or $(i=n\text{ and }b=\mathrm{true})$, and throughout the run satisfies the stated program invariant and keeps every register at most $(|x|+1)$, where $x=\langle 1^n,\operatorname{bits}(i)\rangle$.
hypotheses_covered: Initial state is the test state
Input is the specified self-delimiting encoding
